Introduction 
Viryl Technologies’ WarmTone record presses, with improved mechanical 
design and software monitoring, address some of the challenges of traditional 
automated vinyl record duplication. 
WarmTone Design Features 
The WarmTone design significantly minimizes time required for operator 
intervention and maximizes operating time. 
• The WarmTone’s process settings offer monitoring tools to help you 
make decisions on how to optimize or troubleshoot the record pressing 
process, in the form of real-time monitoring gauges, and historical data 
collection. 
• The WarmTone has fail-safe features which pause operation of 
components to prevent unintended damage of the machine or operator 
injury. For example, the WarmTone stops the feedscrew from turning 
when the pre-plasticizer has not been pre-heated or when the back 
pressure has exceeded safe thresholds. 
• The WarmTone’s processes include timeouts to automatically cool the 
system (most importantly, the pre-plasticizer) if it is left idle for too 
long. 
• The WarmTone Stacking Swing Arm efficiently stacks finished records 
to more than one spindle. Each spindle holds up to 100 finished records, 
and can be removed and replaced while the press is still in operation. 
• The Swing Arm also automatically moves cooling plates from a stack 
and transports them to the finished record stacks every 5 - 10 records 
(as set by the operator) on each spindle. 
• The WarmTone’s pre-loadable label cartridges can hold up to 1000 
labels. You can pre-load all the cartridges required for your press run. 
The WarmTone has a pause function that allows the operator to replace 
the label cartridge without negatively interrupting the processes on the 
machine. This minimizes downtime and allows the operator to fill 
cartridges at more convenient times.

pages.heading: A sensor detects and indicates low levels of resin in the hopper,
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
10 
® 
• A sensor detects and indicates low levels of resin in the hopper, 
allowing the operator to replenish the hopper at the most convenient 
time in the press cycle. In cases where the hopper is critically low, the 
Pre-Plasticizer stops operation to prevent damage to the press. 
• Job and PVC pre-sets catalogue the most effective settings for each pre-
qualified vendor’s PVC, and enables the operator to archive their own 
custom pre-sets. This allows plants to control process variables, 
streamline workflow, and improve overall manufacturing quality. 
• The WarmTone significantly reduces the challenges and time required 
to complete a PVC changeover. The pre-plasticizer hopper can be 
emptied by a handle at the base, leaving only the material within the 
barrel to be purged through the nozzle of the Pre-Plasticizer. This 
design also eliminates the extra time needed to collect and granulate the 
extruded material, and reduces potential loss of recycled material due 
to over-handling, which may introduce debris to the PVC mix. 
• The stampers are secured to the moulds using a hybrid mechanism that 
is easy and time-efficient for the operator. Each stamper is released 
with one twist of the clamp ring and one pull of a mechanism holding 
the centre bushing; each stamper is secured with one twist of the clamp 
ring and one push of the mechanism.

Safety Precautions 
Intended Use 
The WarmTone record press, together with the accompanying ADAPT software 
platform, is used to duplicate large quantities of commercial quality, standard 
12” vinyl music/audio recordings. 
The WarmTone is designed and built for industrial use by trained adult 
personnel. The machine cannot be installed in facilities or structures that are 
mobile, and must not be used in configurations or in combination with 
equipment other than those prescribed in this operation manual. 
The WarmTone must be used only for the purpose for which it was specifically 
designed. All other uses are to be considered incorrect and therefore 
unreasonable. The Manufacturer cannot be held responsible for any damage 
resulting from improper, incorrect, or unreasonable use. 
The Extruder, Press, and Trimmer modules of the WarmTone system are 
intended to be used together, and must never be operated separately. 
 WARNING 
Any improper, incorrect, or unreasonable use or any changes to 
the devices or software shall nullify any sort of warranty claim 
with respect to Viryl Technologies Corp. 
Installation and Service 
The WarmTone must be installed only by Viryl Technologies-authorized 
personnel. Only technically qualified personnel, trained by Viryl Technologies, 
shall perform troubleshooting and service procedures on the software and 
internal components. 
Power Outage 
 WARNING 
In the event of a prolonged power outage, ensure that the 
WarmTone eStop is engaged to prevent unexpected machine 
behaviour when the power resumes.

Dedicated Installation for Software 
The ADAPT Software Platform includes a dedicated PC. This PC is an integral 
component to the overall ADAPT system, including but not limited to the web 
portal service offered to Viryl customers. ADAPT requires a dedicated local 
network connection with access to your service provider’s network. 
Disconnecting power, network connections, or otherwise tampering with 
hardware will nullify any sort of warranty claim with respect to Viryl 
Technologies Corp. 
Installation and Use of Unrelated Software 
Unrelated software applications cannot be installed or used on the computer 
running the ADAPT software, as this may affect performance and compromise 
or corrupt important operational data collected from the WarmTone, which will 
impact the performance of features available in ADAPT. 
Data Backup 
Data backup for ADAPT software is performed via MySQL replication with 
Viryl’s servers, and should not be performed by the client.

Hydraulic Pressing Station 
The finished Puck is shuttled from the pre-mould, together with an Upper and a 
Lower printed record label, into the centre of a Hydraulic Ram, where it will be 
pressed between two Stampers that imprint the A-side and B-side grooves of 
the final record. There is excess plastic material (“Flash” or “Flashing”) 
produced on the periphery of the record. The Flash ensures material properly 
fills all the way towards the outer “Lead in” grooves of the record (i.e. section of 
audible sound or silence before the first audio track during playback). 
Label Cartridges 
Two Label Cartridges are attached to each WarmTone. 
One Label Cartridge feeds labels that attach to the top side of each vinyl record 
(typically the A-side) and the other Label Cartridge feeds labels that attach to 
the bottom side of the record (typically the B-side). 
Each Label Cartridge must be pre-loaded prior to running the machine, and can 
carry up to 1000 labels. 
The Label Cartridges are attached or removed from the machine using the 
thumb latch. 
 
 CAUTION 
The WarmTone contains many sharp edges and potential pinch 
points. Please ensure that you are wearing adequate protective 
safety equipment when you are accessing the machine to change 
labels.

pages.heading: Record Centre Pin
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
30 
® 
Record Centre Pin 
The Record Centre Pin travels vertically (down and up) within the press 
volume. 
The pin is used to grab the Labels and Puck from the Transport, keep them 
centre-aligned, and form the centre hole of the record during pressing. 
Hydraulic Ram 
The Hydraulic Ram has a capacity of 150 tonnes and is used to compress the 
Puck and Labels together and form the grooves of the record. 
The speed of the Hydraulic Ram can be adjusted to optimize record quality. It is 
recommended that only experienced Operators adjust the ram speed. 
WARNING 
The hydraulic ram may make a chattering noise and cause a 
vibration hazard due to air bubbles in the oil feeds. This usually 
occurs due to incorrect speed settings for the ram speed. The 
noise may cause irritation or potential hearing loss over 
prolonged exposure. It is recommended that operators wear 
hearing protection. Please contact Viryl Technologies for technical 
advice if this chattering noise persists or is excessive. 
 
Manifold with Process Valves for Heat/Cool 
The Steam and Water supply pipelines that go to and from your Boiler and 
Chiller are connected to the WarmTone via the Manifold that sits on top of the 
Hydraulic Pressing Station 
The Manifold uses process valves to control which pipelines are open during 
the heating and cooling cycles. 
The Manifold is also equipped with three temperature sensors 
(thermocouples). The thermocouples measure temperature of steam or water 
at 1) the inlet to both moulds, 2) the outlet from the top mould, and 3) the 
outlet from the bottom mould. 
DANGER 
When checking for leaks in the mould fixtures or manifold, please 
stand clear of the WarmTone while running Manual Heat cycles. 
Leaking pipes can expel steam at high pressure. Note that Manual 
Heat will not work if the eStop on the WarmTone is engaged.

pages.heading: Transport Swing Arm
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
31 
® 
Transport Swing Arm 
After the Hydraulic Ram is opened, a robotic Swing Arm transports the pressed 
vinyl record (along with any “Flash” that may still be attached to the record) 
from the centre of the pressing volume to the Trimmer. 
The Swing Arm is equipped with bellowed suction cups to pick up and drop off 
the record.

pages.heading: Trimming and Stacking Station
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
32 
® 
Trimming and Stacking Station 
 
Trimmer 
The Stacking Swing Arm delivers the record to the Trimmer. The record is then 
sandwiched between two platters and a motor turns the platters into a straight 
cutting blade to trim. 
The vinyl record is trimmed to size, removing any “flash” from the pressing 
process. 
The cutting blade is heated to ease trimming (default setting is 65OC / 150OF). 
WARNING 
Please wear heat-resistant protective gloves when servicing or 
handling the knife blade, or clearing excessive trim from the chute.

pages.heading: Stacking Swing Arm
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
33 
® 
Stacking Swing Arm 
The robotic Stacking Swing Arm picks up each finished vinyl record from the 
Trimmer, carries the record, then drops it onto one of the Stacking Spindles. 
The Swing Arm is equipped with bellowed suctions cups to pick up and drop off 
the record (similar to the Swing Arm on the Hydraulic Pressing Station). 
WARNING 
The swing arm can occasionally release a blast of air when it is 
picking up a record, creating an excessive noise. It is 
recommended that operators wear hearing protection to avoid 
hearing damage that may occur over prolonged exposure. To 
prevent this noise, you can disable the Center Blast feature in the 
HMI. Please note that disabling Center Blast may cause vinyl 
sticking issues. 
 
The Stacking Swing Arm also automatically picks up and transports Cooling 
Plates to either Stacking Spindle when required (every 5 to 10 records as set by 
the Operator).

pages.heading: Stacking Spindles
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
34 
® 
Stacking Spindles 
There are two Spindle locations available for stacking finished records. 
Each Spindle has capacity to carry 100 finished records (with cooling plates 
stacked every five to ten records). 
A Spindle can be removed upon request by the operator during specific 
intervals of time while the machine is running. However, at least one Spindle 
must be present at any time while the machine is running.

pages.heading: Cooling Plates
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
35 
® 
Cooling Plates 
The WarmTone is equipped with a location to stack aluminum Cooling Plates. 
Cooling Plates are automatically placed on the finished record stack between 
every 5 to 10 records (as set by the Operator) to draw out heat evenly from the 
stack as the records continue to cool.

pages.heading: Operational Overview
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
36 
® 
Operational Overview 
The following is an overview of the record pressing process of the WarmTone 
machine. 
1. The Pre-mould on the Pre-Plasticizer lowers. 
2. The Pre-Plasticizer motor turns the feedscrew to make a puck. 
3. The Label Cartridges are extended towards the suction cups. 
4. Suction cups use vacuum pressure to grab a label from each Cartridge. 
5. The Pre-mould on the Pre-plasticizer raises. 
6. The Puck and Labels are shuttled by the Transport toward the centre of 
the Hydraulic Ram. 
7. Once in position, the record centre pin comes straight down through the 
centre of the press area and passes through the centre hole of the 
Labels and the Puck. 
8. Vacuum is turned off so that the suction cups release the labels. 
9. The record centre pin holds the Labels and the Puck, and ensures that 
they remain aligned at the centre of the Hydraulic Ram. 
10. The Transport moves back to its original position, ready for the next 
Puck and ready to grab the next set of Labels. 
11. The valves introduce steam to heat the moulds. Note that heating may 
begin earlier in the process to reduce cycle time. 
12. With the Labels and Puck in position, the Hydraulic Ram begins to close 
and compresses the Puck and Labels together. 
13. The Hydraulic Ram holds closed at high pressure (Dwell period). 
14. The valves introduce cold water to cool the moulds. 
15. The Hydraulic Ram opens to release the pressed record, and the centre 
pin raises. 
16. The Transport Swing Arm picks up the record from the centre of the 
Hydraulic Ram and moves it to the trimming station. 
17. The trimmer platters sandwich the untrimmed record. 
18. A straight rectangular blade scissors downward to make an entry cut 
through the Flash. 
19. The trim motor rotates the untrimmed record into the blade to remove 
the Flash and trim the record to its final size. 
20. The trimmer platters open and the Stacker Swing Arm picks up the 
finished record. 
21. The Stacker Swing Arm moves the finished record to one of the two 
available Stacking Spindles.

pages.heading: Label Oven
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
40 
® 
Label Oven 
Depending on the source of the paper labels, they may need to be baked in an 
oven to remove moisture before being loaded into the WarmTone’s label 
cartridges. Baking time and temperature depends on the paper type and 
quality, and on the ink content in the label. A small capacity laboratory grade 
gravity convection oven with forced air is well suited for this operation. 
At minimum, the oven should be able to fit 4-inch diameter labels on a 
horizontally oriented spindle, and treat at least 4000 labels at a time with its 
shelves removed. A maximum temperature of 450°F is sufficient for this 
process. 
Hopper Vacuum (optional) 
The hopper can be optionally fitted with an auto loader unit that automatically 
keeps the PVC level topped up. The WarmTone hopper accepts any “European 
Type” 275 mm DIA flange auto loader. A device such as the Shini SAL-3U is 
ideal. It is powered by a standard wall plug and comes complete with high/low 
sensors. A large container of PVC pellets placed on the floor nearby can be 
loaded into the hopper at a rate of 440 lbs/hour, and does not need to be 
integrated with the WarmTone’s control system. 
Viryl Technologies recommends that you use an automatic PVC loader. Filling 
the hopper manually can increase the risk of personal injury to the operator.

pages.heading: Materials Overview
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
41 
® 
Materials Overview 
Resins 
Virgin PVC Compound 
The WarmTone is designed to process rigid PVC compounds produced for 
pressing records. 
Traditional black compound generally yields better record sound quality than 
colored compounds. 
Please note that the use of unapproved or untested compounds may cause 
deteriorated record quality, damage to the WarmTone machine, and could 
result in voiding your warranty. 
Compound types must not be mixed. 
Please check with Viryl Technologies for the latest approved compounds. 
Note: Once you have decided on a PVC compound that best suits your 
requirements, Viryl Technologies recommends that you continue using that 
compound if possible. 
Processing guidelines should be obtained from the vinyl manufacturer. Please 
note that the WarmTone settings may need to be adjusted due to plant 
conditions such as ambient temperature, humidity, and the critical outputs 
from your boiler and chiller. 
Recycling processed PVC compound 
Non-contaminated PVC trimmings, flash, non-conforming records and un-
pressed ‘pucks’ can be processed with a plastic grinder or ‘granulator’ for re-
use. Pressed records must have their labels punched out prior to re-processing. 
Material must be free of impurities, such as label paper, dirt, metal chips and 
dust. 
Overheated or burnt compound has been destabilized and is not suitable for 
reuse. The granulate particles or ‘regrind’ should be mixed with new PVC 
compound of approximately the same size.

You must filter the regrind to remove the dust or other non-PVC particles

should also be filtered with a magnet to remove any metal filings that can be 
introduced during reprocessing or handling. 
Note: We recommend that you add no more than 10% regrind to virgin 
compound.

Safety Overrides 
• Emergency Stop (eStop) – pressing the eStop on either the Main 
Control Panel, the junction box for the stacker, or the Control Panel 
above the Hydraulic Power Pack will abort any part of the process 
immediately. Press the eStop in the event of an emergency, if you notice

temperature.

pages.text:

® 
Control Pendant (Optional) 
The Control Pendant is a three-button enabling device, and is used to move the 
hydraulics of the press in small increments to allow for maintenance 
procedures such as changing moulds. 
Please note that the Control Pendant is an optional item, and may be purchased 
separately. It is compatible with all WarmTone models. 
To enable the pendant operation, ensure the Control Pendant is connected to 
the right side of the front panel on the WarmTone. On some WarmTone models, 
the Control Pendant attaches to the main hydraulic power panel. Go to the Run 
Screen on the HMI, then press Hydraulic Ram. On the Hydraulic Ram details 
screen press the Pendant button. Apart from the Service/Maintenance Entry 
Door, all other safety access points must be closed. 
 
The pendant has three enabling buttons: 
• A large rectangular trigger button on the handgrip of the pendant. This 
trigger button has two actuating positions. Squeezing the button 
halfway engages the hydraulic override.

pages.heading: A round button on the top of the pendant, which is used to raise the
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
49 
® 
• A round button on the top of the pendant, which is used to raise the 
hydraulic in increments. 
• A round button above the trigger button, which is used to lower the 
hydraulic in increments. 
The three positions of the main (handgrip) button represent three different 
states. Use two fingers to squeeze the handgrip button to its active state. 
State 1 – Resting state 
• The trigger button is not pressed. The process cannot run. 
State 2 – Operating state 
• The trigger button is actuated, pressed halfway into its middle position. 
A green light will notify the operator. The process is now allowed to 
run. 
• The process is stopped if the button is released or pressed all the way 
down to its end position (stopping state). 
State 3 – Stopping state 
• The trigger button is pressed to its third and final position, flush to the 
handgrip. The process will stop in this position. 
• The trigger button must be fully released into “resting state” before 
“operating state” can be reached again. 
After you have completed the maintenance activities using the pendant, close 
the guarding doors and return to normal operation (press the Auto button on 
the Hydraulic Ram Details screen or simply press Start on the Run Screen) on 
the HMI.

not powered on, an Error Action Aborted message will display on the screen.

1. Enter the date in the field in YYYY-MM-DD format. 
2. Press the Retrieve button. The settings from the date are populated in 
the value fields of the screen. 
Load Job 
Pressing the Load Job displays the Machine Settings window, which allows 
you to save job details, compound settings, and other process settings specific 
to previously-saved jobs as a single pre-set. You can select from a list of 
recently saved jobs from the drop-down. You can also Import, Export, upload 
and download specific jobs and process settings from this screen.

pages.heading: About WarmTone
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
60 
® 
About WarmTone 
Pressing About on the Main Menu displays a window which includes the 
WarmTone software version and contact information for Viryl Technologies. 
 
Exit 
This button allows you to exit the WarmTone HMI to a windows-based 
interface. This file system holds, for example, the .csv files for saved job settings. 
It is rare that you will need to exit the WarmTone HMI except to perform 
advanced troubleshooting under the guidance of a Viryl Service Technician.

pages.heading: Workflow Mode – Job Details
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
61 
® 
Workflow Mode – Job Details 
 
This screen allows you to set up the parameters for a new job, including Job 
Number, Description, Job Type, Order Number of Records, Press Number of 
Records, and Compound Settings. 
To enter Job Details: 
1. Touch anywhere on a field you wish to edit. A keypad pops up on the 
screen, allowing you to populate that field. 
2. Populate the fields with the specifics of the press run: 
• Job #/IRSC code (required) 
• Description (optional) 
• Job Type – select one of the following from the drop-down menu: 
• Test Presses – for testing the quality of the stampers and 
general pressing quality before the production run. 
• Production – the main run for the pressing. 
• Testing – for troubleshooting issues with the performance of 
the press. 
Job details will transfer to the ADAPT system to help track jobs in 
progress and completed per press, which helps monitor overall 
plant operation.

pages.heading: Comment (optional) – use this field keep notes specific to your
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
62 
® 
• Comment (optional) – use this field keep notes specific to your 
press run. 
• Order # of Records – Enter the total number of records ordered by 
the customer. 
• Press # of Records – Enter the number of records you want to 
manufacture on the WarmTone, including extra records in case 
some fail later at sound or cosmetic QC inspection. The Operator 
must manually adjust this number at his/her own discretion before 
or during the press run. Please note that you do not need to account 
for records spoiled in mid-process, which are not counted towards 
the Record Count. 
• Compound Settings – Click on the Compound Settings field to 
invoke the Compound Settings list. Select a desired pre-set name 
from the drop-down menu. Clicking ACCEPT in this screen 
associates the machine settings from the selected file with your 
current job.

pages.heading: Alternatively, you can recall the job details and process settings used for a
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
63 
® 
Alternatively, you can recall the job details and process settings used for a 
previously saved job: 
1. Press Load Job on the Job Details screen to access a list of recently 
saved jobs, and select a job from the drop-down. The screen that 
appears is like the Manage Process Settings screen, but includes the job 
parameter specifics from the previously saved job. 
 
2. Review the Entry Name and Value fields for the job. 
3. If the values are appropriate, press ACCEPT to restore the job details 
and process settings associated with the job selected. 
Note: Any current process settings that you may have set may be overwritten 
by pressing the ACCEPT button. Be sure you want to use the Values shown 
before pressing ACCEPT. 
By default, the Job Details and all process settings on the HMI are autosaved 
daily, and every time a job completes. You can restore those values using the 
Load Job button. If you wish to save Job Details and process settings at other 
points in time, press Save Job to load the settings into memory for future use. 
You can use the Export Jobs button to save the Job Details and settings to a 
*.csv file with a custom name. This feature is available for advanced users to, for 
example, save and transfer settings to another WarmTone press. 
Note: Please ensure that all components of the WarmTone are powered 
on before loading or saving any job or process settings.

pages.heading: Workflow Mode – Warm Up
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
64 
® 
Workflow Mode – Warm Up 
 
Press Start Warmup to initiate the warm-up cycle, which: 
• Automatically heats the pre-plasticizer zones to pre-set temperatures as 
dictated by the selected Compound Setting (or custom set points for 
each zone temperature). The Pre-Plasticizer Zone Temperatures will 
begin heating Zones 1, 2, 3, and Die Zone to set point temperatures 
• Initiates the Soak Time counter after the pre-set temperatures are 
reached, as indicated on screen. Soak Time (five-minute default) 
ensures that the Zones hold temperatures for a minimum amount of 
time per setting so that zone temperatures stabilize. 
• Heats the Trimmer knife blade to a pre-set temperature. 
The Machine State ribbon in the upper portion of the screen indicates the 
current warm-up state. 
If required, press Cancel Warmup to exit the warm-up cycle. 
You may also press the Fault button to view any faults that may occur during 
the warm-up process. This button will flash red if system faults are detected. 
Once Soak Time is complete, as indicated on screen, the Purge button is 
enabled. Press Purge to begin the purge cycle. Refer to page 111 for more 
details with respect to purging the WarmTone.

pages.heading: Press Purge again to end the purge cycle.
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
65 
® 
Press Purge again to end the purge cycle. 
At this point, the Operator should observe the quality of the PVC mixture being 
extruded from the Pre-plasticizer. If necessary, create a few pucks and check 
the quality and weight of the extruded PVC, as well as the puck size and density. 
If necessary, you can press Pre-Plasticizer Details Screen to access the Pre-
Plasticizer sub-screen. For more details on the options available on this sub-
screen, refer to page 71. 
The Heat Cycle Test button allows the WarmTone to validate the steam and 
water settings for the flow into the moulds. The test results may provide 
feedback about the operation of your steam and cold water lines, which may 
inform you about operation of your boiler and/or chiller. If the test fails, check 
that the boiler and/or chiller systems are turned ON, and that all shutoff valves 
above the WarmTone manifold are open. 
If necessary, you can press Heat/Cool Details Screen to access the Heat/Cool 
Valves sub-screen. For more information on the options available on this sub-
screen, refer to page 82. 
The Trimmer area of the screen displays a readout for the knife blade 
temperature. 
If necessary, you can press the Trimmer Details button to access the Trimmer 
Details sub-screen. For more details on the options available on this sub-screen, 
refer to page 88. 
Once the Trimmer knife reaches the set temperature, and the Purge and Warm 
Moulds cycles are completed, the operator may proceed to Run Mode.

pages.heading: Workflow Mode – Run
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
66 
® 
Workflow Mode – Run 
 
The main operation phases for the WarmTone occur during the Run Mode. 
If Warm Up has completed successfully, job parameters and system settings 
have been loaded, and the machine is running without issues, there is little that 
the operator needs to do during the Run Workflow Mode except to press Start 
and wait until the record stacks are full or the job is complete. 
On the Run Screen, the Start button is enabled (flashing), which indicates that 
the machine is ready to run. 
1. Press Start. 
2. The Machine State band in the upper portion of the screen will indicate 
the current state of the press (eg. Machine Is Operating, Machine Is Idle, 
etc.). 
3. Press the Stop button at any point during Run to end the pressing cycle. 
The machine will automatically come to a stop once all in-progress 
records are completed. 
Should any issues occur, the WarmTone will stop and prompt you to address 
the issue. The Fault button on the Run Screen will flash. To resume pressing, 
the Faults must be cleared on the interface.

pages.heading: The Job Status button allows you to view the current state of the press run.
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
67 
® 
The Job Status button allows you to view the current state of the press run. 
Pressing the Job Status button calls up a popup screen: 
 
This popup allows you to change the number of records in the press run. 
Pressing Continue allows the run to resume with the adjusted number. End 
Job allows you to quit the current press run. 
The Time Remaining Before Auto Cooldown is a countdown readout that 
monitors the WarmTone idle time. When the displayed number reaches zero, 
the machine will automatically enter shutdown mode. 
If you wish to monitor details about any element of the machine, adjust specific 
settings manually (to resolve a fault or to customize settings), press the 
appropriate button on the Run Screen to open any of the following sub-screens: 
• Pre-Plasticizer 
• Labels and Transport 
• Heat/Cool Valves 
• Hydraulic Ram 
• Swing Arm 
• Trimmer 
Note: The WarmTone software places these sub-screens into Diagnostic Mode 
after initial power up. If the screens are in Diagnostic Mode, the navigation 
buttons, as well as the Start button, will appear in orange on the Run Screen. 
All elements must be in Auto Mode to start the Run Workflow. To switch these 
sub-screens to Auto Mode, you can go to each appropriate sub-screen to change 
each element to Auto Mode, or you can press the Start button to switch all sub-
screen zones to Auto mode and to begin the run process.

pages.heading: Process Details
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
68 
® 
Process Details 
The Process Details button on the Run Screen displays a detailed window of 
the heat/cooling timing relative to timing of the press and other mechanisms, 
allowing you to visualize the effect of your timing adjustments to the overall 
process. Any adjustments you make update the Projected Cycle Time. 
 
This screen shows color-coded bars which show the WarmTone process in real 
time. The slider moves along the bar and indicates the current point in the 
sequence. 
The information boxes on this screen correspond to the color-coded slider. 
Above the slider are indicators that show the current heat and cooling timings 
for the moulds. Below the slider are boxes that indicate the timings for 
mechanical actions of the machine. 
The two white arrow indicators on the bar indicate the remaining amount of 
heat time in seconds after the press has closed. This is known as the Cycle 
Offset and is represented by the number in the unmarked box located near the 
arrows. 
 WARNING 
Do not adjust the Process Settings unless you are an experienced 
press operator. Incorrect adjustment to timing can result in 
damage to the stampers and may cause damage to parts of the 
WarmTone.

pages.heading: The following timings can be adjusted manually by pressing the setting
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
69 
® 
The following timings can be adjusted manually by pressing the setting 
number: 
• Heat 
• Dwell 
• Cool Moulds 
• Press At Pressure 
• Closing Speed Setpoint – as a percentage 
• Pressure Setpoint – in psi 
Other timings are for information only and depend on settings for other 
components of the WarmTone. Some aspects may be out of the operator's 
control, or may vary cycle to cycle.

pages.heading: Press At Pressure Details
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
70 
® 
Press At Pressure Details 
Pressing the Press At Pressure button displays a detail screen which allows you 
to make fine adjustments to the Press Dwell Time. The Heat Dwell, Cool Moulds, 
and Cycle Offset values are automatically calculated (not editable on this 
screen) to help you understand their impact on Press Dwell. 
The Minimum Allowed Dwell Time is a baseline value and cannot be adjusted. 
The WarmTone software will not allow you to calculate a Dwell Time below this 
value. 
We recommend that you use the Auto Calculate Dwell Time button on this 
window.

pages.heading: Pre-Plasticizer Details
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
71 
® 
Pre-Plasticizer Details 
 
The Pre-Plasticizer Details window allows you to override the set points for the 
barrels and other heat settings, as well as to review the set points for other 
features in the Pre-Plasticizer Zone of the WarmTone. 
You can also initiate a purge of the Pre-Plasticizer by pressing the Purge 
button. 
This screen also includes navigation buttons which allow you to jump to the 
Run Screen or the Fault Screen. You can also use the arrow buttons to move 
through all the other sub-screens of the Run Screen. 
Temperature Set Points 
The details area of the window includes temperature gauges for: 
• Barrel Zone 1 
• Barrel Zone 2 
• Barrel Zone 3 
• Die Zone 
• Melt Temperature 
• Premould 
This area also includes indicators which display the current temperature for the 
zones.

pages.heading: By touching the set point temperature indicator, located at the bottom of the
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
72 
® 
By touching the set point temperature indicator, located at the bottom of the 
temperature gauge, you can adjust the set point for that zone. Press Enter to 
commit your new settings in the HMI. 
Note: There is a pre-set temperature limit of 350F for the pre-plasticizer heat 
zones. Ensure that you double-check your manual heat entries in the HMI 
before committing them to the WarmTone. 
Puck Size Setting 
Allows you to make minor adjustments to the puck size, if the pre-trimmed 
records do not have enough flash to be efficiently transported to the trimmer. 
Use the Larger/Smaller buttons to change the puck size. 
Torque and Pressure Details 
There are four indicators at the bottom of the window, which display: 
• Feedscrew RPM 
• Motor Torque Percentage 
• Melt Pressure (expressed in PSI) 
• Feedthroat Temperature 
Manual Pre-Mould Control 
The Pre-Plasticizer screen also allows you to manually Retract or Extend the 
Pre-Mould mechanism to perform maintenance. This functionality can only be 
accessed when the WarmTone has been placed in Diagnostic Mode. 
Save Compound Settings 
The Save Compound Settings button displays a popup screen which allows you 
to save your settings with a unique file name, or to load previously-saved 
settings from the drop-down list. This functionality is like that available in the 
Compound Settings window as described on page 56.

pages.heading: Pre-Plasticizer Advanced Settings (Maintenance Level access only)
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
73 
® 
Pre-Plasticizer Advanced Settings (Maintenance Level access only) 
 
When you are logged in with Maintenance level access, press the Advanced 
Settings button on the Pre-Plasticizer Details screen for the following settings: 
• Idle Timeout Time Setpoint (in seconds) 
• Soak Time Setpoint (in seconds 
• Operating Speed Reference (in RPM) – corresponds with Screw Speed 
Setting on the Pre-Plasticizer Details screen. 
• Purge Speed Reference (in RPM) 
• Puck Size Settings, which can be set using either: 
• Puck Size Premould Reed Switch FBK control method: 
• Maximum Extrude Time (for Reed Switch Feedback) 
• Minimum Extrude Time (for Reed Switch Feedback) 
• Puck Size Setpoint (extra time) 
• Puck Size Fixed Time Setpoint control method: 
• Extrude Time Setpoint (for Fixed Time) 
• Startup Puck Size Additional Time (for Fixed Time) 
• Startup Puck Number (total # of pucks for Fixed Time). 
 
CAUTION 
Please note that Pre-Plasticizer Advanced Settings should only be 
adjusted by experienced Operators.

pages.heading: Labels and Transport Details
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
74 
® 
Labels and Transport Details 
 
The Labels and Transport Details screen allows you to manually isolate and 
adjust mechanical functionality on the labeller and transport. The WarmTone 
must be in Diagnostic Mode for this screen to be activated. 
This screen also includes navigation buttons which allow you to jump to the 
Run Screen or the Fault Screen. You can also use the arrow buttons to move 
through all the other sub-screens of the Run Screen.

pages.heading: The following functions can be tested by touching the corresponding area on
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
75 
® 
The following functions can be tested by touching the corresponding area on 
the screen: 
• Extend Transport 
• Retract Transport 
• Upper Vacuum On/Off 
• Lower Vacuum On/Off 
• Top Label Cylinder Raised/Lowered 
• Lower Label Cylinder Raised/Lowered 
• Center Pin Extended 
• Center Pin Retracted 
The Ret and Ext fields turn green when the WarmTone sensors identify 
successful retraction and extension of the corresponding components. 
If these fields do not activate (turn green) when in the correct retracted or 
extended position, check the LED on the corresponding physical sensor on the 
WarmTone. 
If the LED is OFF, you can adjust the sensor’s position manually. Using a small 
flathead screwdriver, loosen the screw at the front of the sensor, then adjust the 
sensor cable by hand. 
If the LED is ON, there may be a wiring issue between the front control panel 
and the sensor.

pages.heading: Labels and Transport Advanced Settings
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
76 
® 
Labels and Transport Advanced Settings 
Clicking Advanced Settings on the Labels and Transport Details screen 
displays a popup widow which allows you to further isolate the label and 
transport functions for testing. 
 
The following functionality is available: 
• Labels Enabled (default) – Allows you to cycle the press with labels. 
• Label-Less Mode Enabled – Allows you to cycle the press without 
applying labels to the pucks 
• Top Labels Only 
• Bottom Labels Only 
• Puck Detect Sensor Enable 
• Puck Detect Sensor Disable – please use this option only if necessary. 
For example, you may want to consider disabling this sensor to 
continue operations if a fault recurs when pucks are correctly forming 
and being transported correctly through the press.

pages.heading: Hydraulic Ram Details
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
77 
® 
Hydraulic Ram Details 
 
The Hydraulic Ram Details screen allows you to isolate and test the hydraulics 
on the WarmTone. 
This screen also includes navigation buttons which allow you to jump to the 
Run Screen or the Fault Screen. You can also use the arrow buttons to move 
through all the other sub-screens of the Run Screen. 
There are three modes available on this screen: 
• Pendant Mode – allows you to incrementally move the hydraulic up or 
down for testing or maintenance purposes, using the hand-held 
pendant with the service/maintenance entry open. For more details on 
how to use the pendant, refer to page 48. Please note that the Pendant is 
an optional item. 
• Auto Mode – allows you to invoke the Manual Sequence Request button 
on this screen, which tests the hydraulic ram in the run state. 
• Diagnostic Mode – allows you to perform specific tests on the 
components of the hydraulic ram, including incrementally moving the 
hydraulic up or down. 
The Press Temperature Hydraulic Oil displays the current temperature of 
the oil in the press hydraulics.

pages.heading: The following information is available in the Sequence Settings area:
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
78 
® 
The following information is available in the Sequence Settings area: 
• Press Dwell SP (setpoint) controls how long (in seconds) the press is 
held closed at high pressure. Please ensure that this setting is equal to 
or longer than the combined time of Heat Dwell plus Cool Time on the 
Heat/Cool Valves Details screen. 
• Press Force Setpoint (from Ram Pressure)– in tonnage 
• Ram Pressure Setpoint – in psi 
• Close to Pressure Speed – expressed as a percentage of maximum 
speed. 
• Switch to Pressure Position – in inches 
The following functions are available on this screen in Diagnostic Mode: 
• Hydr Motor state – indicates whether the motor is on or off. 
• Hydr Motor Press To Start – push to turn on the motor for the press 
(Note: this will not move the bolster). 
• Hydr Motor Press To Stop – push to turn off the motor for the press. 
• Main Ram state – indicates whether the hydraulic ram is in the up or 
down position. 
• Main Ram Press To Move Up – holding this button will move the ram 
up. The ram will stop moving and maintain its current position when 
you release the button. 
• Main Ram Press To Move Down – holding this button will move the 
ram down. The ram will stop moving and maintain its current position 
when you release the button. 
There are also two warning indicators on this screen: 
• Safeties OK/Not OK – Indicates when the eStop is engaged. 
• Control Power On/Not On – Indicates that the WarmTone is in either 
Manual mode (On) or Auto mode (Not On). 
The Press Trend and Press Manual Move Settings buttons display additional 
windows, allowing the operator to further adjust the settings on the hydraulics. 
These windows are only accessible when you are logged in with Maintenance 
level access.

pages.heading: Press Trend Screen (Maintenance Level access only)
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
79 
® 
Press Trend Screen (Maintenance Level access only) 
The Press Trend screen is useful for troubleshooting your press pressure. 
 
The Press Trend screen displays a graph of the Pressure and Displacement 
(Position) of the hydraulics, mapped over time (in tenths of a second). This 
information includes: 
• Master Pressure 
• Last Pressure 
• Master Displacement 
• Last Displacement 
The Use Last As Master button allows you to assign the Last Pressure and Last 
Displacement trends as the master.

pages.heading: Press Manual Move Settings Screen (Maintenance Level access only)
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
80 
® 
Press Manual Move Settings Screen (Maintenance Level access only) 
 
The Press Manual Move Settings screen includes the following adjustable 
parameters: 
• Manual Close To Pressure 
• Manual Close To Position 
• Manual Open To Bottom 
• Pendant Close To Pressure (can only change speed) 
• Pendant Close To Position (can only change speed) 
• Pendant Open To Bottom (can only change speed)

pages.heading: As shown on the screen, the specifications for these positions include:
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
81 
® 
As shown on the screen, the specifications for these positions include: 
• Speed Percentage 
• Pressure (in psi) 
• Pressure (in Tons) (informational only) 
This screen retains the following information/functionality from the Hydraulic 
Ram Details screen: 
• Actual Ram Position 
• Ram Pressure (in psi) 
• Ram Pressure (in Tonnage) 
• Ram Position Adjust buttons 
WARNING 
The hydraulic ram may make a chattering noise and cause a 
vibration hazard due to air bubbles in the oil feeds. This usually 
occurs due to incorrect speed settings for the ram speed. The 
noise may cause irritation or potential hearing loss over 
prolonged exposure. It is recommended that operators wear 
hearing protection. Please contact Viryl Technologies for technical 
advice if this chattering noise persists or is excessive.

pages.heading: Heat/Cool Valves Details
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
82 
® 
Heat/Cool Valves Details 
 
The Heat/Cool Valves Details screen allows you to monitor the manifold 
temperatures and pressures for steam and water entering and exiting the press 
moulds. You can also override the Heat Sequence Settings to adjust timing for 
the Steam and Water process valves. 
This screen also includes navigation buttons which allow you to jump to the 
Run Screen or the Fault Screen. You can also use the arrow buttons to move 
through all the other sub-screens of the Run Screen. 
Heat Sequence Settings 
You can override the following pre-set Heat Sequence Settings (in seconds) in 
Diagnostic Mode for the pressing sequence: 
• Heat – the time in which the moulds are heated. 
• Dwell – the time after the Hydraulic Ram reaches maximum pressure 
before the cooling of the moulds begins. 
• Cool – the time in which the moulds are cooled. 
Note: Adjusting the Cool time will impact not only the temperature at the end 
of the current cycle but also the temperature at the start of the subsequent 
cycle. If you try to adjust the Cool time for any reason, you may also need to 
adjust the Heat time.

pages.heading: WARNING
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
83 
® 
 WARNING 
Do not adjust the Heat Sequence Settings unless you are an 
experienced press operator. Incorrect adjustment to timing can 
result in damage to the stampers and may cause damage to parts 
of the WarmTone. 
 
Manual Functions 
In Diagnostic Mode, you can use the Heat Moulds (steam) and Cool Moulds 
(water) fields to manually validate the fluid flow into the moulds. These fields 
will create a flow to the WarmTone for as long as you hold them down. 
The Manual Sequence Request, which runs in Auto Mode only, allows the 
WarmTone to cycle through heating and cooling functionality.

pages.heading: Valve and Mould Temperature Indicators
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
84 
® 
Valve and Mould Temperature Indicators 
The lower section of the Mould Temperature Details screen is a visual depiction 
of the pipes carrying the fluids into and out of the pressing moulds. Information 
includes the maximum and minimum temperatures and pressures measured 
during the last complete cycle. 
• Inlet Temperature Indicators – These values display the 
temperatures of the steam (heating) and water (cooling) as they flow 
into the moulds. The upper value is for steam and the lower value is for 
water. 
• Outlet Temperature Indicators – These values display, for the top and 
bottom moulds, the temperatures of the condensed steam (condensate) 
and water as they flow out of the moulds. For each mould, the upper 
value is for condensate and the lower value is for water. 
o If the indicators are displayed in grey, the temperatures are 
within acceptable range based on your last calibration. 
o If the indicators are displayed in orange, the temperatures are 
too low based on your last calibration. 
o If the indicators are displayed in red, the temperatures are too 
high based on your last calibration. 
• Press the Temperature Trend button to display the heat variances in 
the moulds for the last 20-minute period. 
• The Calibrate button allows you to save the current temperature 
readings on the screen as a baseline.

pages.heading: Mould Temperature Advanced Settings (Maintenance level access only)
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
85 
® 
Mould Temperature Advanced Settings (Maintenance level access only) 
 
When logged in with Maintenance level access, press Advance Settings to 
specify timings for the following functions: 
• Cold Water Purge – a short period at the start of heating during which 
the water drain process valve is opened to expel any warm water 
remaining from the previous cooling cycle back to the chiller loop. 
• Steam Build – a short period after heating during which all process 
valves are closed to allow steam to sit within the moulds. 
• Steam Purge – a short period at the start of cooling during which the 
condensate drain valve is opened to expel any residual condensate from 
heating back into the condensate tank. 
• Dual Drain – a short period during which both condensate and water 
drain process valves are opened. 
 CAUTION 
It is strongly recommended that you do not change the Mould 
Temperature Advanced settings unless you are very experienced 
with the steam and chilling systems, or are instructed to do so by 
Viryl Technologies authorized personnel. Changing the values 
incorrectly may cause damage to parts of your supporting 
infrastructure either immediately or over time.

pages.heading: Swingarm Transport Details
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
86 
® 
Swingarm Transport Details 
 
The Swingarm Transport Details screen allows you to manually isolate 
mechanical functionality on the swingarm for the sequence of transporting the 
record from the press to the trimmer. The WarmTone must be in Diagnostic 
Mode for this screen to be activated. 
The Centre Blast Enable/Disable button allows you to control the air blast 
that is transmitted from the swing arm during pickup of the record. 
 
WARNING 
The swing arm can occasionally release a blast of air when it is 
picking up a record, creating an excessive noise. It is 
recommended that operators wear hearing protection to avoid 
hearing damage that may occur over prolonged exposure. To 
prevent this noise, you can disable the Center Blast feature in the 
HMI. Please note that disabling Center Blast may cause vinyl 
sticking issues. 
 
This screen also includes navigation buttons which allow you to jump to the 
Run Screen or the Fault Screen. You can also use the arrow buttons to move 
through all the other sub-screens of the Run Screen.

pages.heading: Manual Settings
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
87 
® 
Manual Settings 
The following functions can be activated and tested by touching the 
corresponding area on the screen: 
• Push RC Top On/Off 
• Push RC Bottom On/Off 
• Top Airknife On/Off 
• Bottom Airknife On/Off 
• Swingarm Vacuum On/Off – The FBK (feedback) button is active 
(green) when the suction cups are picking up records. 
• Raise Swingarm 
• Lower Swingarm 
• Center Blast On/Off – air blast transmitted from the swing arm during 
the pickup of the record. 
The Manual Sequence Request, which runs in Auto Mode only, allows the 
WarmTone to cycle the swingarm through the transport sequence. 
The following set points may be incrementally adjusted by Operators with 
Maintenance Level access. Please note that the Transport Set Points may only 
be adjusted on the HMI on certain WarmTone models. 
• Press 
• Standby 
• Trimmer

pages.heading: Trimmer Details
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
88 
® 
Trimmer Details 
 
The Trimmer Details screen allows you to manually isolate mechanical 
functionality for the trimming and stacking sequence of the WarmTone. The 
WarmTone must be in Diagnostic Mode to activate these features. 
This screen also includes navigation buttons which allow you to jump to the 
Run Screen or the Fault Screen. You can also use the arrow buttons to move 
through all the other sub-screens of the Run Screen. 
The following functions can be tested by touching the corresponding area on 
the screen: 
• Spin Trimmer Plate/Stop Trimmer Plate 
• Raise Cylinder To Trim Position 
• Lower Cylinder To Home Position 
• Knife Cut/Knife Standby 
• Raise Cooling Plate Stack – The FBK button is active (green) when the 
WarmTone sensors identify successful raising of the Cooling Plate 
stacks. 
• Lower Cooling Plate Stack – The FBK button is active (green) when 
the WarmTone sensors identify successful lowering of the Cooling Plate 
stacks.

pages.heading: Stacker Vacuum On/Off - The FBK button is active (green) when the
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
89

Workflow Mode – Shutdown 
 
The Shutdown Workflow Mode is initiated by the operator and prepares the 
WarmTone for machine shut down. The Shutdown Mode turns off all 
operations and actively cools the Pre-Plasticizer, Trimmer knife, and the 
moulds (if necessary). 
Shutdown is also initiated if the machine has been left idle (in Standby Mode) 
for a predetermined time. The time remaining before shutdown is visible 
(expressed in seconds) on the Run Screen. This time restriction is a safety 
precaution due to hazards associated with leaving the Pre-Plasticizer heated 
too long. If this occurs, the Shutdown screen will appear and the Cool All 
Systems field is activated. The operator can intervene during the shutdown 
period by manually restarting the WarmTone (pressing Warmup on the Warm 
Up screen). The subsequent Warmup time sequence depends on the machine 
state of the shutdown when it is halted.

Installing and Removing Stampers 
Viryl supplies a customized stamper removal tool to use when replacing 
stampers, as shown below. 
 
Before attempting to remove or install the stampers: 
• Ensure that the machine has stopped running and that the bottom 
bolster is down. 
• Manually cool the moulds for at least 10 seconds. 
• It is recommended that you remove any jewellery (eg. bracelets, rings) 
to prevent accidental scratching of the stampers or moulds. 
• Press the eStop on the WarmTone to prevent any part of the machine 
from actuating. 
• Close the shutoff valve for the main air line into the system. Release any 
air from the system. 
• Unlatch and swing the Trimmer/Stacking Assembly away from the 
hydraulic on the press until you have sufficient access to the mould 
area. 
 DANGER 
The WarmTone safety system prohibits entry to the machine until the 
machine has stopped operation, power is disconnected and the machine 
is disabled. Under no circumstances should the safety system be 
bypassed. If the safety system is bypassed, sudden mechanical 
movement of the components could result in serious injury to 
personnel. 
 
WARNING 
Potential pinching and crushing hazards are present when opening the 
Trimmer access point for maintenance activities. Please ensure you are 
wearing protective gear and avoid wearing loose clothing or jewelry. 
 WARNING 
 
Removing the stamper clamp ring can present a pinching hazard. Please 
wear protective gloves when removing or replacing the stamper rings.

pages.heading: WARNING
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
102 
® 
 WARNING 
The sharp edges of the pushing mechanisms present a pinching and 
cutting hazard. Safety measures must be followed and protective 
clothing must be worn when removing the stampers. 
 
Removing stampers 
1. Place a protective mat over the bottom stamper. Begin removing the top 
stamper as follows. 
2. Ensure that the pusher mechanisms, located near the air nozzles, are 
fully extended. Push down to extend for the upper stamper, up to 
extend for the bottom stamper. 
3. Loosen the retaining screw on the stamper lock bar. 
4. Using the stamper removal tool, insert the end of the tool with the twin 
screws into the corresponding holes on the stamper clamp ring. Gently 
turn the ring until the notch on the ring aligns with the side pin on the 
mould. Carefully remove the ring by hand. 
5. Insert the end of the stamper removal tool into the stamper lock bar 
and, while supporting the center bushing and stamper, pry the lock bar 
away from the moulding. The mechanism that secures the center 
bushing and stamper will loosen and the bushing can be removed. 
Carefully remove the stamper and bushing. 
6. Repeat steps 2 to 5 for the bottom stamper. Carefully lift the stampers 
by the edges to remove the stamper and the bottom centre bushing. 
Installing stampers 
1. Clean the front of the stamper with a residue-less solvent (e.g. acetone, 
isopropyl alcohol) and a microfiber cloth. 
2. Carefully wipe the mould face and backs of the stamper with a 
microfiber cloth and residue-less solvent to ensure that the surfaces are 
free of dust or any other particles. 
3. Place the stamper over the mould face and insert the centre bushing all 
the way into the centre hole of the mould. While the bushing is in place, 
gently tap the end of the stamper lock bar until the center bushing is 
flush with the stamper. 
4. Place the stamper clamp ring over the skirt of the stamper. 
5. Using the stamper removal tool, insert the end of the tool with the twin 
screws into the corresponding holes on the stamper clamp ring, turning 
it counter-clockwise until it locks into place.

pages.heading: 6. Tighten the retaining screw on the stamper lock bar.

6. Tighten the retaining screw on the stamper lock bar. 
7. Ensure that the pusher mechanisms near the air nozzles are back in 
place, and that the air knives (if applicable) are pointed so that air will 
shoot out slightly clear of the stamper clamp ring. 
8. Repeat 1-6 with remaining stamper. 
9. Open the air shut-off valves. 
10. Close all access points on the WarmTone. 
You must press the Resume push button before the machine can operate again. 
Press the Start button on the Run Screen on the HMI to resume pressing 
operations. 
Removing and Replacing Moulds 
Ensure the machine has stopped running and is in Diagnostic Mode, the 
emergency stop is engaged, and the bottom bolster is down before attempting 
to install or remove moulds. 
 DANGER 
The WarmTone safety system prohibits entry to the machine until the 
machine has stopped operation, power is disconnected and the machine 
is disabled. Under no circumstances should the safety system be 
bypassed. If the safety system is bypassed, sudden mechanical 
movement of the components could result in serious injury to 
personnel. 
 DANGER 
The moulds weigh approximately 75 pounds each. It is recommended 
that two people perform these procedures, to ease with carrying and 
safely positioning the moulds. 
 WARNING 
Please ensure that you are wearing proper safety equipment such as 
gloves and boots to prevent injury from heated pipes/hoses and water, 
and to protect from potential injury from a dropped mould. 
 
WARNING 
Potential pinching and crushing hazards are present when opening the 
Trimmer access point for maintenance activities. Please ensure you are 
wearing protective gear and avoid wearing loose clothing or jewelry. 
WARNING 
 
Removing the stamper clamp ring can present a pinching hazard. Please 
wear protective gloves when removing or replacing the stamper rings.

104

 WARNING 
The sharp edges of the pushing mechanisms present a pinching and 
cutting hazard. Safety measures must be followed and protective 
clothing must be worn when removing the stampers. 
 WARNING 
Always handle moulds with nitrile gloves. Residual skin oils left on the 
mould surface can cause serious problems with the sound quality of 
your pressings. If moulds are handled improperly, clean them 
thoroughly with a solvent (eg. Acetone) and wipe dry before using. 
 
Before Removing Moulds 
When preparing to remove moulds, please follow these steps: 
1. Allow the press to complete its final cycle by pressing the “Stop” button 
on the Run Screen. 
2. On the HMI, go to the Heat/Cool Valves Details screen. 
3. Press and hold the “Cool Moulds” button for three 30 -second intervals 
to cool the moulds down. 
4. Press the eStop. 
5. Shut off all four process valves on the plumbing manifold. 
6. Unlatch and swing the Trimmer/Stacking Assembly away from the 
press. 
Removing Moulds 
1. Remove any stampers, stamper clamp rings, and centre bushings 
according to the procedures starting on page 101. 
2. Remove the finger plate from the pusher assemblies, located on either 
side of the moulds. There is a single screw holding the finger plate to the 
pusher assemblies. Hold the pusher assembly gently with a wrench and 
use an Allan key to remove the screw from the finger plate. Lift the 
finger plates away from the pusher assemblies. 
3. Unhook the process hoses from the mould quick disconnects. 
4. Collect any leftover water in the moulds and hoses. 
5. Beginning with the top mould, place the mould jig in the machine, 
locating it on the two dowel pins on the bottom carrier, mould dowel 
pins toward the extruder. 
6. Close the trimmer door, and clear the faults in the HMI. 
7. Go to the Hydraulic Ram Details screen and switch to Diagnostic mode. 
8. Start the press motor, and raise the bolster manually in the HMI until 
the mould jig is just touching the top mould. If you raise the bolster too

9. Press the eStop and swing the Trimmer to the open position. 
10. Loosen the four strap clamp bolts on the top mould carrier until the 
inserts can be easily removed from the clamping indents on the side of 
the mould. Make sure the strap clamp bolts are entirely clear of the 
mould. 
11. Close the trimmer door, and clear the faults in the HMI. 
12. Go to the Hydraulic Ram Details screen and switch to Diagnostic mode. 
13. Lower the bolster in the HMI, ensuring that the top mould is lowering, 
resting on the jig. 
14. Open the Trimmer door. 
15. Remove the top mould and the mould jig from the bolster. 
16. If you are replacing the moulds, replace the top mould according to the 
procedure on page 106. 
 
17. Loosen the four strap clamp bolts on the bottom mould carrier, 
beginning with the most difficult to access. Slide the strap clamps out 
from the mould insert, ensuring that the clamp bolts are clear of the 
mould face. 
18. Lift the bottom mould from the bolster.

pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY

Installing Moulds 
1. Ensure process valves on the pipe manifold above the press are closed. 
2. Engage the eStop and open the Trimmer assembly to access the press. 
3. Remove the pusher mechanisms. 
4. Inspect the surface of the top and bottom mould carriers. If there is 
significant rusting on the mounting surface, apply a rust removing 
solution and manually wipe or sand (no less then 150 grain) the 
affected areas. It is imperative that this surface is completely flat. 
5. Inspect the bottoms of both moulds. If there is significant rusting on the 
mounting surface, apply a rust removing solution and manually wipe or 
sand (no less then 150 grain) the affected areas. It is imperative that 
this surface is completely flat. 
6. Remove any mould protectant used for storage or shipping from the 
surfaces of the moulds. Moulds must be absolutely clear of this material 
before installation. Please refer to the Mould Care instructions on page 
133 for more details. 
7. If any of the above components are rusted beyond cleaning or still 
tangibly uneven after rust removal, they must be reworked (by Viryl 
Technologies) or replaced. 
8. Carefully wipe and dry all components to remove all moisture and 
visible particles. 
9. Place the bottom mould on the carrier. 
10. Secure the bottom mould with the strap clamps. 
11. Place the mould jig on top of the bottom mould, with the guide pins 
facing up and closer to the extruder.

mould back towards the extruder until it is stopped by the pins. 
13. Close the Trimmer and disengage the eStop. Clear the faults in the HMI. 
14. Go to the Hydraulic Ram Settings in Diagnostic mode in the HMI, start 
the motor, and slowly move the top mould up until the orange fiberglass

raise the bolster slowly if the mould and disc remain free to move (i.e. 
are not being pinched).

16. Close the Trimmer door and start the press motor. 
17. Drop the bolster 1/2" using the Hydraulic Ram Details screen in the

18. Check that the mould is securely in place before dropping the bolster

19. Press the eStop and swing the Trimmer to the open position. 
20. Remove the mould support tool. 
If the mould is not secure, remove the top mould according to the 
procedure on page 104 and restart the mounting process. 
21. Engage the emergency stop and follow the same cleaning and mounting

23. Once both moulds are secure and properly aligned, attach the feed and

pages.heading: Purging
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
111 
® 
Purging 
Purging is the process of mixing the PVC to the correct heat and consistency 
before the press run. 
 
 
Purging is also required in the following instances: 
• When switching from one compound type or colour to another. 
• When compound has been overheated, and destabilized in the barrel. 
• If the pre-plasticizer has been idle for a pre-determined time. 
• When clearing the barrel of resin for maintenance. 
Purging extrudes vinyl resin by slowly rotating the screw (slower than typical 
operating speed) to ensure that all material within the barrel mixes evenly. 
BARREL 
INTERNAL FEEDSCREW

pages.heading: You can initiate purge by pressing the Purge button on the Warmup Screen. To
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
112 
® 
You can initiate purge by pressing the Purge button on the Warmup Screen. To 
end purge, you must press Purge again. Purge is complete once the consistency 
of vinyl exiting the nozzle is pliable (soft and starts to thin in diameter), the 
material is hot (unable to touch even with heat-resistant gloves for longer than 
approximately 3 seconds), and flows freely. 
 CAUTION 
Operation of the Pre-Plasticizer, including Purge, should never be 
conducted until Soak Time is complete. By default, the WarmTone 
prevents the operator from purging until a minimum Soak Time of 
5 minutes is completed. 
It is good practice to always conduct a Purge whenever starting up the Pre-
Plasticizer at the beginning of the day or after extended idle periods (> 15 
minutes or sometimes more frequently). By default, the WarmTone prevents 
operators from entering Run mode without completing a Purge after 
approximately 60 mins of Standby Mode. 
Purging is performed by using one of many commercially available purge 
compounds, which is a base plastic compound mixed with additives. Depending 
on the type of purge compound used, instructions may vary. Contact the 
compound manufacturer for details. 
Changing Resins (Clean Changeover) 
The following procedure allows you to purge the WarmTone hopper of any old 
resins from the system. This procedure can be performed any time the operator 
needs to change vinyl color for the pressing. 
1. Ensure the machine has stopped running before opening the hopper 
drain. 
2. Turn off the vacuum loading system (if applicable). 
3. Open the hopper drain by slowly pulling on the handle (located above 
the Pre-Plasticizer feed throat) to regulate the flow of compound still 
left in the hopper. Collect the excess compound in a clean container 
until the hopper is empty. 
WARNING 
The hopper handle has sharp edges and potential pinch points. 
Always wear safety gloves when emptying the hopper drain.

pages.heading: 4. Wipe the inside of the hopper to remove any remaining pellets.
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
113 
® 
4. Wipe the inside of the hopper to remove any remaining pellets. 
DANGER 
You must disconnect power to the Pre-plasticizer if you are 
removing the hopper for cleaning. Ensure that you keep your 
hands clear of the Pre-plasticizer feedthroat when removing the 
hopper. 
 
5. Close the hopper drain by pushing the handle until the bottom cavity of 
the hopper is flush with the feed throat inlet and the hopper body is 
completely upright. 
6. Manually load the hopper with purge compound through the loading 
hatch at the top of the Pre-Plasticizer. 
7. Press the purge button on the warm-up tab to start the purge process. 
Collect the extrusion in a clean, heat resistant container. 
8. Immediately after purging begins, set the Pre-Plasticizer zone 
temperatures to the purge manufacturer’s specifications by accessing 
the Pre-Plasticizer tab from the run screen on the HMI. 
Ensure the motor torque does not exceed 90% and the extrusion 
pressure remains under 2600 PSI. If the torque or pressure exceeds 
these values, stop purging and increase all zone temperatures by 10 F. 
Wait for temperature readings to increase before restarting purge. If the 
readings continue to exceed the given values, power down the machine 
and contact Viryl service. 
9. Monitor level of purge in hopper using sight glass, ensuring purge 
compound is always visible in the hopper. 
10. Continue to purge until extrusion turns the color of the purge 
compound, and all traces of the previous compound are gone. Refill the 
purge compound in the hopper if necessary. Purging generally requires 
less than half a hopper of purge compound. 
11. When extrusion is made up of purge compound only, stop the Pre-
Plasticizer and empty the hopper according to steps 3 to 5. 
12. Begin refilling the hopper with the new PVC compound by powering up 
the vacuum loader or refilling the hopper manually through the hatch. 
13. Set the Pre-Plasticizer zone temperatures according to the 
manufacturer’s specifications for the new compound. 
14. Once zone temperatures are within 20F of settings, purge the Pre-
Plasticizer.

pages.heading: 15. Monitor the motor torque and extrusion pressure on the pre-plasticizer
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
114 
® 
15. Monitor the motor torque and extrusion pressure on the pre-plasticizer

pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY

® 
Cleaning Procedures 
General Cleaning 
All areas beneath and around the WarmTone should always be kept clean and 
free of debris. 
Sweep under the stacker/trimmer module several times during each press run. 
Any debris under the wheels of this module can unbalance the machine, causing 
mechanical damage and potentially affecting the quality of your pressing. 
Stampers 
Ensure that new stampers are cleaned with a diluted cleaning fluid, and wiped 
dry with a lint-free cloth. Particles on the surface of the stamper can affect the 
pressing quality. 
When replacing stampers, ensure that there are no dust particles or any other 
debris between the stamper and the mould. Particles can damage the moulds, 
and affect the pressing quality. 
Mould Care 
Steam and water are a necessary part of the record pressing process. Extended 
contact with water causes corrosion damage to steel. 
NOTE: Mould corrosion, rust, and surface damage from improper 
handling or operator error are NOT covered by your warranty! Mould 
damage can be prevented by following these guidelines. Proper care and 
maintenance are necessary to ensure the longevity of the moulds. 
These Mould care guidelines must be strictly observed to maintain maximum 
pressing quality and functionality for your WarmTone. The top surfaces of the 
moulds are critical and easily scratched or dented. The durability of the 
WarmTone record moulds rely on Operators and Pressing Maintenance staff to 
understand and adhere to these guidelines. 
Handling Moulds 
Always handle moulds with nitrile gloves. Any residual skin oils on the surfaces 
of your moulds will damage the mould surface finish and negatively impact the 
sound quality of your pressings. If moulds are handled with bare hands they 
must be thoroughly cleaned with solvent (eg. acetone) and dried before use.

pages.heading: Moisture on Moulds
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
134 
® 
Moisture on Moulds 
Moulds in use (or in storage) must always be kept dry. If any leaks occur in or 
around the moulds, stop your current processes immediately to address the 
issue. Corrosion on the mould surfaces will cause immediate and long-term 
problems with your press. 
Pay attention to ensure that water does not get between the stamper and the 
mould profile, or the mould bottom and the carrier plate. If there is water 
leaking into those areas we highly recommend that you clean and dry the 
mould immediately, even if it requires removing the mould from the press. 
Before removing moulds: 
1. Allow the press to complete its final cycle by pressing the “Stop” button 
on the Run Screen. 
2. On the HMI, go to the Heat/Cool Valves Details screen. 
3. Press and hold the “Cool Moulds” button for three 30-second intervals 
to cool the moulds down. 
4. Press the eStop. 
5. Shut off all four process valves on the plumbing manifold. 
6. Follow the mould removal procedure as outlined on page 103. 
Shipping and Storing Moulds 
If you have swapped out a mould, please use the following guidelines to safely 
store the mould. This procedure also applies to preparing the moulds for 
shipping. 
1. Flush as much water from the moulds by “swishing” the mould so that 
most of the water can drain from the ports. 
2. Plug the ports to block any residual water from leaking. Hole 
inlet/outlets are -08 JIC 37 Flare. 
3. Wrap the plugs on the mould with Plumbers/Teflon tape. 
4. Line the wooden mould crate with VCI plastic (the blue plastic from 
shipping). 
5. Coat the mould with WD-40 (or equivalent) to prevent rusting. Do not 
wipe down. 
6. Wrap the thoroughly soaked mould in the VCI plastic and seal the crate 
for shipment/storage. 
7. If storing, store flat in a cool dry environment.

Heavy accumulations of dust and other debris on the surface and in the

ventilation can lead to the motor overheating and premature motor failure. 
These surfaces can be cleaned out with a vacuum. 
Fan Filters 
The fans servicing the power panels must be cleaned every two weeks when 
the WarmTone is in regular use. There are 14 filters in total. 
Before accessing the fans, ensure that the machine has stopped running and is 
in Diagnostic Mode, and the emergency stop is engaged. 
1. Pull the fan cover down to access the fan filters. 
2. Remove the filter from the fan housing. Do not attempt to clean the 
filter while it is still in the housing. 
3. Clean the dust from the fan with a low-powered vacuum, or shake the 
dust free by hand. 
4. Replace the filter and close the fan housing.

pages.text:

Oil Level Gauge 
 
A hydraulic oil level gauge is used to fill the hydraulic reservoir to the correct 
level. Incorporated in the level gauge is a low level shut off switch. If the oil 
level gets low the hydraulic motor will shut off and an alarm will appear on the 
HMI screen. The hydraulic motor will not start again until the hydraulic oil level 
in the reservoir is replenished. 
Thermocouple 
A thermocouple is used to monitor the hydraulic oil in the tank. If the oil 
temperature exceeds the maximum setting the hydraulic motor will shut off. 
DANGER 
In the event of an oil leak from any of the hydraulic lines, hit the 
eStop on the press and shut the machine down. Leaked oil is a 
potential ignition hazard. Under high pressure, leaking hose can 
expel atomized oil into the air, creating a serious fire hazard.

Suction Cups 
Suction cups are used on the Trimmer swing arms and on the Transport. These 
wear items will need to be replaced occasionally on-site. 
Replacing Trimmer Swing Arm Manifold Suction Cups 
There are three suction cups mounted on each of the swing arms: the transport 
swing arm and the stacking swing arm. The method of removing and replacing 
them is the same. 
To remove and replace the swing arm suction cups: 
1. Enter Diagnostic Mode in the HMI. 
2. Extend the swing arm in the HMI. 
3. Power down the WarmTone and engage the eStop. 
4. Open the Trimmer safety door. 
5. Move the Swing Arm into position. 
6. Loosen the screws holding the suction cups using a flat-head 
screwdriver. 
7. Remove the suction cups from their mounts. 
8. Push the replacement suction cups over the mounts and tighten the 
screws. 
9. Inspect and test for air leakage by running a few records and ensuring 
that the Swing Arm is picking up the records correctly. 
Transport Label Suction Cups 
There are eight label suction cups are located on the transport. These items are 
high wear and will need to be replaced in the field occasionally. 
To remove and replace the Transport label suction cups: 
1. Extend the transport in the HMI. 
2. Pull the suction cups from their fittings. 
3. Insert the new suction cups directly onto the fittings. 
4. Test for suction and air leakage by manually triggering the suction in 
the HMI and ensuring that the cups are properly picking up labels.
