pages.heading: Glossary of Terms
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
199 
® 
Glossary of Terms 
ADAPT (Advanced Device Analytics Pressing Technology) – Viryl’s 
proprietary software program that allows pressing plants to track press output 
and productivity. 
Cooling Plates – Metal plates that are placed in stacks of finished records in the 
Trimming Station (usually every five to ten records) to expedite the cooling 
process. 
Cooling Stacks – The two areas in the Trimming Station where finished 
records are placed for cooling. 
eStop – Emergency safety button on the WarmTone that immediately shuts 
down all machine operations. 
Fill/Non-Fill – Terms that describe how well the PVC is distributed over the 
entirety of the finished record, ie. Are all the grooves filled in a uniform fashion? 
Flash – The extra vinyl that is trimmed away from the edge of the pressed 
record. 
Guarding System – Plexiglass panels that surround the WarmTone and 
prevent inadvertent Operator access to the machine. The Guarding System’s 
doors cannot be opened unless the WarmTone’s eStop button is engaged. 
HMI (Human Machine Interface) – The Operator’s touch-screen digital 
control panel for the WarmTone. 
Hopper – Container which holds the raw PVC pellets, and feeds the pellets into 
the pre-plasticizer. 
Knife Cylinder – The mechanism in the Trimming Station that controls the 
heated trimming knife, and regulates the air flow and heat to the knife.

pages.heading: Manifolds – There are two types of manifolds referenced on the WarmTone:
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
200 
® 
Manifolds – There are two types of manifolds referenced on the WarmTone: 
The Pipe Manifold is located at the top of the press and refers to the cluster 
of valves that control the flow of water and steam to the hydraulics and 
moulds of the WarmTone. 
Air Manifolds are located on the top of the hydraulic section of the press, 
and on top of the Trimming Station. These manifolds control the air flow to 
the pre-mould, swing arms, transport, knife cylinder, and suction cups. The 
manifolds are easily accessed for testing and maintenance purposes. 
Mould – Metal forms that support the stampers on the hydraulic, where the 
puck is pressurized into a flat record. 
PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) – Term for the computing system that 
runs the WarmTone, and is present in the electrical panels. 
Pre-Mould – The area where the pre-plasticizer extrudes the PVC to form the 
puck. 
Pre-Plasticizer – Device that heats and extrudes the raw PVC, often called the 
extruder. 
Press Dwell – Indicates how long the hydraulic on the press stays closed at 
high pressure. 
Puck (or Biscuit) – The initial form of the PVC after it is extruded from the pre-
plasticizer and shaped by the pre-mould. The PVC is formed into a dense 
circular shape and aligned with the labels before being transported to the 
hydraulic press. 
Purge – the process where the pre-plasticizer is cleared and cleaned of PVC 
compound. This occurs as a part of general maintenance, and before any PVC 
resin changeovers (for new colors etc.). 
PVC (or Vinyl) – the raw material used to make records. 
Soak Time – A setting for the Pre-Plasticizer that ensures that the barrels 
(zones) hold temperature for a pre-determined minimum period before the 
temperatures stabilize. The WarmTone soak time default is five minutes.

pages.heading: Stamper – Nickel-plated metal discs that contain the ‘positive’ image of the
pages.text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY 
 
201 
® 
Stamper – Nickel-plated metal discs that contain the ‘positive’ image of the 
pressed record. 
Swing Arm – There are two swing arms on the WarmTone: 
The Transport Swing Arm moves the pressed record to the Trimming 
station. 
The Stacker Swing Arm moves the trimmed record from the Trimmer 
station to the Cooling Stacks. 
Transport – The mechanism on the WarmTone that shuttles the PVC form 
through the machine, from puck to pressed record. 
Trimming Station – The module of the WarmTone where the finished records 
are transported for flash trimming, then stacked and cooled
